subject: SLA baseline % and monthly remediation roadmap for Greenridge
messages:
From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: elaine.wu@greenridge.com, ops@greenridge.com, procurement@greenridge.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline % and monthly remediation roadmap for Greenridge

Hi Elaine / Greenridge team,

Thanks again for the productive discovery call this week. Per our conversation I’m sharing a proposal for the standard SLA band we typically include in enterprise templates and a remediation (monthly credit) schedule that maps to downtime bands. This is intended as a starting point for negotiation — we can carve out exceptions for scheduled maintenance, known-batched inference windows, and capacity ramp events.

Highlights (proposal v1 attached):
- Service availability baseline: 99.95% per month (applies to hosted API endpoints).
- Latency objective: p95 <= 450ms for standard request profile (exceptions for batched inference and large-sequence workloads).
- Monthly remediation: tiered credit slabs tied to percentage of monthly invoice (detailed in attachment). Suggested cap: 10% of monthly invoice for production accounts; alternate lanes available for different pricing.
- Carveouts proposed: scheduled maintenance windows (we propose a 4-hour monthly maintenance allowance), major capacity migration windows, and behavior caused by overloaded client-side patterns.

Two negotiation levers we recommend for Greenridge:
1) Offer a 99.9% "discounted lane" with a higher credit cap (e.g., 12.5%) if Greenridge prefers headline availability to be lower for cost savings.
2) Keep 99.95% as our standard for customers on the performance tier — limit monthly credits there via a per-incident slab with an overall cap.

Please review the attached Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1.pdf. If you want, we can run a 60-day pilot on a split traffic routing where a portion of traffic uses the discounted lane to validate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Next steps: can you confirm procurement and legal points of contact and any internal carveouts you require (e.g., internal maintenance blackout windows)? Happy to take a redline or hop on a quick call.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 18 pages)
From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@greenridge.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenridge.com, ops@greenridge.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline % and monthly remediation roadmap for Greenridge

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear summary and the proposal. A few quick reactions from our side after an internal sync:

- Greenridge infrastructure is heavily batch-oriented for nightly scoring. That workload tolerates higher latency, but we need clearer carveouts for batched inference windows so we don’t trigger credits during predictably high-latency periods. Please call this out explicitly.
- On availability, our procurement asks that the headline SLA be 99.9% (public-facing), with the understanding that we can have an internal performance lane for critical paths. The ask is motivated by our budget constraints — 99.95% is preferred but may push us out of budget.
- Regarding credits: we prefer a dollar-cap approach (fixed dollar monthly cap) rather than a percent of invoice in the short term. It makes forecast modelling easier for our finance team.
- Procurement will also require SOC 2 Type II evidence and an audit trail of change management for any service-side schema changes.

Can you send a redline with two options: (A) 99.95% with the credit slab you proposed, and (B) a 99.9% headline SLA with a fixed monthly credit cap (please propose an example cap amount for a mid-size account)? Also include a clear batched-inference carveout section.

Elaine
Director, Platform Operations
Greenridge Financial

Attachment: Greenridge_SLA_Notes.docx (DOCX, 2 pages)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: elaine.wu@greenridge.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, procurement@greenridge.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline % and monthly remediation roadmap for Greenridge

Elaine — thanks for the candid feedback. A few clarifications and a compromise path that should address Greenridge procurement/finance modeling needs while protecting our operational margin.

1) Batched inference carveout: we’ll add an explicit clause that defines a batched-inference window (configurable on a per-account basis). During declared batched windows (e.g., nightly scoring 01:00–05:00 local time) latency SLOs are relaxed and those periods are excluded from uptime calculations if declared at least 72 hours in advance or discovered via the mutual action plan pilot.

2) Dual-lane approach (recommended):
- Performance lane (Standard): 99.95% availability, p95 latency <= 450ms, monthly credits tiered and expressed as percent-of-invoice with a 10% cap.
- Value lane (Discounted): 99.9% availability, relaxed latency objective, and a fixed-dollar monthly remediation cap. For a mid-size account of Greenridge’s scale we would propose a $50k/month cap as an example; this is adjustable based on committed spend.

3) Fixed-dollar example: we’ll include the $50k example in the redline but mark it as negotiable — we can map it to a sliding scale as spend changes.

4) Compliance: SOC 2 Type II artifacts and a short change-management evidence bundle are standard for enterprise procurement; we’ll attach SOC 2 scope and offer to run an evidence collection call with your security team.

I’ve updated the proposal to reflect the two-lane option and an explicit batched-inference carveout. I’m attaching Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1b.pdf which includes sample language and both lane options.

If this looks acceptable, we can draft a redline for legal to review and include a short mutual action plan that sequences pilot traffic, observability hooks (tracing + token-level latency), and a DocuSign path for signature.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Proposal_v1b.pdf (PDF, 20 pages)
From: procurement@greenridge.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: elaine.wu@greenridge.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline % and monthly remediation roadmap for Greenridge

Laura / Priyom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for adding the batched-inference carveout. Procurement is comfortable moving forward with a short pilot on the Value lane (99.9% + $50k fixed monthly cap example) provided we receive a redline and SOC 2 evidence package.

Next steps for us:
- Please upload the redline to DocuSign and share the link (we’ll need to route to our legal team).
- Send SOC 2 evidence and a 30-minute evidence call invite for this week.
- We’ll start a 60-day mutual action plan once DocuSign is in flight and the pilot config is agreed (we expect to route ~30% of traffic to the Value lane during the pilot).

Procurement (Greenridge)
